edits.old: circle circumference
edits.new: square perimeter

edits.old: Using 3.14 for π, what is the circumference of a circle with diameter 10 cm?
edits.new: The perimeter of a square photo frame is 56 cm. What is the length of one side?
28 cm
14 cm
16 cm
52 cm

edits.old: Circumference = πd = 3.14 × 10 = 31.4 cm.
edits.new: A square has four equal sides, so each side is 56 ÷ 4 = 14 cm. A divides by 2 as if only two sides counted, C divides the 40 but then appends the leftover 6 (10 + 6 = 16), and D subtracts 4 instead of dividing by 4.

edits.old: uses radius as diameter; computes area
edits.new: divides perimeter by 2; subtracts instead of dividing

edits.old: circle area
edits.new: composite rectangle area

edits.old: Using 3.14, area of radius 6 cm?
edits.new: An L-shaped hallway floor is made of two rectangles: one is 9 m by 4 m and the other is 5 m by 3 m. What is the total area of the floor?
21 m²
36 m²
98 m²
51 m²

Add the two rectangle areas: 9 × 4 = 36 and 5 × 3 = 15, so 36 + 15 = 51 m². A adds the four dimensions instead of multiplying, B counts only the first rectangle, and C multiplies the combined lengths by the combined widths (14 × 7 = 98).

edits.old: circumference; uses diameter
edits.new: adds dimensions; ignores one rectangle

edits.old: logical estimation—square root
edits.new: logical estimation—closest whole-number square

edits.old: Which value is closest to √130?
edits.new: Which whole number multiplied by itself gives a product closest to 130?

11 × 11 = 121 is only 9 away from 130, while 12 × 12 = 144 is 14 away. A rounds 130 down to the benchmark 100 = 10 × 10, C picks the first square past 130 without comparing distances, and D comes from 130 ÷ 10.

edits.old: halves 130; chooses nearest perfect-square root without estimating
edits.new: uses 100 as benchmark; picks square above without comparing distances

edits.old: estimation—square root
edits.new: estimation—between perfect squares

edits.old: A square garden has area 190 square meters. Which is the best estimate of one side length?
edits.new: A square rug has an area of 190 square feet. Its side length, in feet, is between which pair of consecutive whole numbers?
9 and 10
12 and 13
14 and 15
13 and 14

edits.old: √190 lies between 13 and 14 and is about 13.8; A, B, and C are farther from the needed square root.
edits.new: 13 × 13 = 169 and 14 × 14 = 196, and 169 < 190 < 196, so the side is between 13 and 14. A halves 190 instead (9² = 81 and 10² = 100 surround 95), B stops after seeing 12² = 144 fall below 190, and C treats 14 as the lower bound once 14² passes 190.

edits.old: divides area by two; chooses nearest integer without estimating
edits.new: halves instead of using squares; brackets off by one

edits.old: probability—without replacement
edits.new: probability—single draw (or event)

edits.old: A box holds 3 silver and 5 black tokens. Two tokens are drawn without replacement. What is the probability both are silver?
edits.new: A box holds 4 silver, 7 gold, and 9 copper coins. One coin is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is silver or gold?

edits.old: The probability is 3/8 × 2/7 = 6/56 = 3/28; A assumes replacement, B gives only the first-draw probability, and C uses an incorrect second factor.
edits.new: There are 4 + 7 + 9 = 20 coins, and 4 + 7 = 11 of them are silver or gold, so the probability is 11/20. A uses only the silver coins (4/20 = 1/5), B uses only the gold coins, and C gives the probability of copper—the very coins the draw must avoid.

edits.old: assumes replacement; adds probabilities
edits.new: uses one category only; picks the excluded category

edits.old: probability—without replacement
edits.new: probability—single draw (greater-than event)

edits.old: A box has 3 red and 5 blue counters. What is the probability of drawing two blue counters without replacement?
edits.new: A box holds cards numbered 1 through 15. One card is drawn at random. What is the probability that the number drawn is greater than 9?

edits.old: The probability is 5/8×4/7=20/56=5/14; the distractors assume replacement, add probabilities, or use one draw.
edits.new: The favorable cards are 10 through 15—six of the 15—so the probability is 6/15 = 2/5. A counts the nine cards that are 9 or less (9/15 = 3/5), B wrongly includes the 9 itself (7/15), and D drops one favorable card (5/15 = 1/3).

edits.old: assumes replacement; single-draw probability
edits.new: counts the complement; boundary error with greater than

edits.old: geometry reasoning—regular polygon interior angle
edits.new: geometry reasoning—straight-line angle ratio

edits.old: A floor tile is a regular octagon. What is the measure of each interior angle?
edits.new: Two angles together form a straight line. One angle is 4 times as large as the other. What is the measure of the larger angle?

edits.old: The interior-angle sum is (8−2)×180=1,080°, and 1,080÷8=135°; distractors use other polygons or exterior angles.
edits.new: The two angles total 180° and make 5 equal parts, so the smaller is 180 ÷ 5 = 36° and the larger is 4 × 36 = 144°. A stops at the smaller angle, B divides 180 by 4 instead of 5, and C uses 90° as the total (4 × 18 = 72).

edits.old: uses exterior angle; wrong polygon formula
edits.new: reports smaller angle; divides by 4; uses 90 as total

edits.old: adds denominators; fails to simplify
edits.new: adds numerators and denominators; adds numerators without converting

edits.old: One angle of a right angle is 27°. The other is:
edits.new: Two angles are complementary. One angle measures 27°. What is the measure of the other angle?
Complementary angles total 90°, and 90−27=63°; C subtracts from 100, D subtracts from 180, and A slips by ten.

edits.old: 4.75 × 6 = 28.50; A adds rather than multiplies, C misplaces a digit, and D overcounts.
edits.new: 4.75 × 6 = 28.50. A multiplies only the dollars (4 × 6 = 24) and appends the 75 cents, C swaps the cents digits of 28.50, and D rounds to $5 × 6 = $30 and then adds the 75 cents back.

edits.old: At least one = 18 + 15 − 7 = 26, so neither = 32 − 26 = 6; A subtracts incorrectly, B reports the overlap, and D forgets to subtract the overlap before finding neither.
edits.new: At least one activity = 18 + 15 − 7 = 26, so neither = 32 − 26 = 6. A follows an addition slip in totaling 18 + 15 (35 − 7 = 28, then 32 − 28 = 4), B repeats the 7 who do both, and D counts the instrument-only students (18 − 7 = 11) instead of those doing neither.

edits.old: Volume = 7 × 4 × 3 = 84 cubic feet. B omits height, C omits width, and D multiplies incorrectly.
edits.new: Volume = 7 × 4 × 3 = 84 cubic feet. B multiplies only length and width (7 × 4 = 28), while C and D first add all three dimensions (7 + 4 + 3 = 14) and then multiply by the height (14 × 3 = 42) or the length (14 × 7 = 98) instead of multiplying all three dimensions.

edits.old: Subtract 7 to get 5x = 35, then divide by 5 for x = 7. A divides too soon, C adds instead, and D fails to undo addition.
edits.new: Subtract 7 from both sides to get 5x = 35, then divide by 5 for x = 7. A divides 35 by the constant 7 instead of by 5, C follows a subtraction slip (42 − 7 taken as 45, giving 45 ÷ 5 = 9), and D adds 7 to 42 before dividing (49 ÷ 5).

edits.old: Box A holds 30 books on 5 shelves. Box B holds 42 books on 7 shelves. Which statement is true?
edits.new: The first box holds 30 books on 5 shelves. The second box holds 42 books on 7 shelves. Which statement is true?

edits.old: Box A holds more per shelf.
edits.new: The first box holds more per shelf.

edits.old: Box B holds 2 more per shelf.
edits.new: The second box holds 2 more per shelf.

edits.old: Box B holds 12 more per shelf.
edits.new: The second box holds 12 more per shelf.

edits.old: Both rates are 6 books per shelf; comparing totals alone suggests B, but per-shelf rates are equal.
edits.new: Both rates equal 6 books per shelf (30 ÷ 5 = 6 and 42 ÷ 7 = 6). A assumes fewer shelves means more on each shelf, C reports the difference in shelf counts (7 − 5 = 2) as a per-shelf difference, and D does the same with the totals (42 − 30 = 12).

edits.old: 2/5=4/10, and 7/10−4/10=3/10; the distractors subtract denominators, report a used amount, or add.
edits.new: 2/5 of the tank = 4/10, so 7/10 − 4/10 = 3/10 remains. B subtracts the denominator 5 from the numerator 7 (2/10 = 1/5), C subtracts the numerator 2 without converting (7/10 − 2/10 = 5/10 = 1/2), and D adds 2/10 instead of subtracting (9/10).

edits.old: 2(16+w)=54, so 16+w=27 and w=11; the distractors subtract one length or confuse half-perimeter with width.
edits.new: Half the perimeter is 54 ÷ 2 = 27, so the width is 27 − 16 = 11. A reports only how much longer the length is than the width (16 − 11 = 5), B subtracts one length from the whole perimeter and halves what is left (54 − 16 = 38, then 19), and C subtracts both lengths but forgets to halve (54 − 32 = 22).

edits.old: Multiply independent choices: 3×4×2=24; the distractors add categories or omit one category.
edits.new: Multiply the independent choices: 3 × 4 × 2 = 24. A adds the three numbers (3 + 4 + 2 = 9), B multiplies shirts by pants but then only adds the hats (12 + 2 = 14), and C multiplies the shirts by the sum of pants and hats (3 × 6 = 18).

edits.old: adds choices; omits a factor
edits.new: adds choices; mixes multiplying and adding

edits.old: One lap is 2(30+18)=96 m, and 1.75×96=168 m; distractors give one lap, use area, or mishandle the fraction.
edits.new: One lap is 2 × (30 + 18) = 96 m, and 1 3/4 × 96 = 168 m. A stops after one lap, B adds only one more 30 m side for the extra three-quarters of a lap (96 + 30 = 126), and C runs 1 1/2 laps instead of 1 3/4 (1.5 × 96 = 144).

edits.old: area-perimeter confusion; ignores fractional lap
edits.new: stops after one lap; mishandles the fractional lap

edits.old: Triangle angles total 180°, so 180−52−61=67°; the distractors use 90° or incomplete subtraction.
edits.new: Triangle angles total 180°, so 180 − (52 + 61) = 180 − 113 = 67°. D stops at the sum of the two given angles (113°), while A and C come from misadding 52 + 61 (as 123 or 103) before subtracting from 180°.

edits.old: subtracts from 90; arithmetic slip
edits.new: reports the two-angle sum; addition slips before subtracting

edits.old: Volume=8×6×5=240 cm³; the distractors add dimensions, omit one dimension, or make a product error.
edits.new: Volume = 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 cm³. A finds only the top and bottom faces (2 × 48 = 96), and B and C are slips in the final step 48 × 5: misreading 48 as 38 gives 190, and taking 200 + 4 × 5 instead of 200 + 8 × 5 gives 220.

edits.old: omits a dimension; adds dimensions
edits.new: computes partial surface area; multiplication slips

Replacement items keep the original key letter and difficulty tag: DGN-MA-023 (B/M), M01-MA-021 (D/M), M01-QR-035 (B/M), M02-QR-035 (D/M), M02-QR-015 (D/H), M03-QR-036 (C/H), M03-QR-031 (D/H). Field 'correct' is untouched throughout.

Template-collision checks run against all 508 bank items: the square-perimeter reverse (P/4), additive L-shape (vs M02-MA-024's subtractive composite), closest-square and between-squares estimation (distinct solve patterns, and M02-QR-035 no longer near-duplicates M03-QR-028), or-event coins vs threshold cards (distinct from each other, from DGN-QR-011/M02-QR-006/M03-QR-008 complements, and from factor/multiple single-draw items), and straight-line ratio angles (two-step, distinct from DGN-QR-037/M02-QR-032 one-step 68-degree items, M03-MA-022, and M01-MA-023).
M02-QR-035 replacement: all four options now share one numeric format (pairs of consecutive whole numbers), removing the only-decimal-key cue.

DGN-MA-005: option B changed from 6/15 (which equaled option A, 2/5) to 1/2, the result of adding numerators without converting thirds ((5+1)/12); it differs from A, C, D and the key. The rationale never referenced option B, so it is unchanged.
M01-MA-023: stem rewritten as a complementary-angles item; options and key verified still correct (90-27=63 at B) and rationale expanded to gloss C (100-27), D (180-27), and A (ten-slip).

The 'misconceptions' field is not present in bank.json; its 'old' values are byte-exact from the ANSWER KEY sheet (column MISCONCEPTIONS) of mock.xlsx at each item's key_row. Rationales for M02-MA-016, M03-MA-022, M03-MA-024, M02-MA-003, M02-QR-023, M03-QR-003, and M03-QR-035 previously claimed error paths that do not produce the printed distractors (e.g. 'omits width' giving 42, 'uses 90' giving 57/77, 'adds' giving 24.75, 'uses area' giving 126); each replacement gloss was verified to land exactly on its option value.
